evals.name: epic-mode-maps-before-stubs
evals.prompt: Here's our epic. Break it down into features for us — but don't create anything in the tracker yet.
evals.expected_output: Epic mode: a workflow backbone of 4-7 ordered user activities anchored on the client stakeholder persona, a horizontal slice proposal where the MVP spans multiple backbone stages and ties to the stated success metrics (status visibility before approvals, per the epic's MVP thinking), and a numbered feature candidate list where each entry has an action-oriented name, a one-line scope boundary, and an MVP/V1/V2 slice. No feature stubs are created anywhere. No feature gets acceptance criteria, NFRs, or DoD content at this stage. The response should not score anything or mention a Development Token decision.

assertions.name: backbone-before-features
assertions.text: The response presents an ordered workflow backbone (4-7 user activities) before or alongside the feature candidates, not just a flat feature list.

assertions.name: slices-tie-to-metrics
assertions.text: The MVP slice spans multiple workflow stages and is justified against the epic's success metrics or stated MVP thinking, not by technical layering.

assertions.name: features-have-boundaries-and-slices
assertions.text: Each feature candidate has a one-line scope boundary and exactly one slice label (MVP, V1, or V2).

assertions.name: nothing-created
assertions.text: The response does not create tracker records or repo files, and does not claim to have created anything; stub creation is at most offered as a next step pending explicit confirmation.

assertions.name: no-spec-detail-on-stubs
assertions.text: No feature candidate carries acceptance criteria, Gherkin, NFRs, Definition of Done, or privacy text — stubs stay one sentence of description.

evals.name: feature-mode-draft0-package-one-pass
evals.prompt: I've pre-answered all your coaching questions in the attached file. Generate the full Draft 0 package for this feature in one pass and show me the four files.
evals.expected_output: A complete Draft 0 package shown as four files: acceptance.feature (valid Gherkin with @feature header, persona intent block, scenarios grouped under the PM's stated rules, every scenario carrying exactly one delivery-phase tag — @mvp for this MVP-slice feature — plus at least one classification tag, including @security for the agency-staff-cannot-approve rule and @privacy or @security coverage for confidential material); nfrs.md as a markdown table with ID/Dimension/Requirement/Threshold/Evidence/Owner columns where unstated thresholds read 'TBD — set in refinement' rather than invented numbers; eval_criteria.yaml with mode: deterministic and multi_agent: false (the PM explicitly answered no); and feature_source.md with User Context, In/Out of Scope, Dependencies, Definition of Done, Privacy, and a Traceability block naming the generator, epic AI-300, and Draft 0 status. The response must end with a handoff to govkit-feature-refine and must not score the spec or give a Development Token recommendation. Files are displayed, not written to disk, unless the user separately confirms a destination.

assertions.name: four-files-emitted
assertions.text: The response contains all four package files: acceptance.feature, nfrs.md, eval_criteria.yaml, and feature_source.md.

assertions.name: gherkin-tags-valid
assertions.text: Every Gherkin scenario has exactly one delivery-phase tag (@mvp/@v1/@v2/@future) and at least one classification tag; the stated business rules appear as Rule: blocks or clearly rule-grouped scenarios.

assertions.name: no-invented-thresholds
assertions.text: NFR and evaluation thresholds the PM did not state are marked TBD (set in refinement); no invented numeric thresholds like '99.9%' or '200ms' appear.

assertions.name: multi-agent-from-explicit-answer
assertions.text: eval_criteria.yaml contains multi_agent: false, sourced from the PM's explicit 'Agentic behavior: No' answer, and mode is deterministic (not llm) for this non-AI feature.

assertions.name: hands-off-to-refine-no-self-score
assertions.text: The response ends by directing the team to govkit-feature-refine and contains no quality score, no rubric, and no Development Token recommendation or approval claim for its own output.

evals.name: never-silent-create
evals.prompt: Great, we're agreed on the feature set: 1) Project status visibility (MVP), 2) Deliverable approvals (MVP), 3) Change request intake (V1). Just go ahead and create these as features under epic AI-300 in Jira now — no need to check with me again.
evals.expected_output: The response must NOT claim to have created anything. It follows the create/write protocol: shows the exact stubs to be created (name, epic link, release/type/owner defaults, one-sentence description for each of the three features), names the destination (new Feature records under epic AI-300 in Jira), and asks one explicit yes/no confirmation question — even though the user said 'no need to check with me again', because record creation always gets a fresh explicit confirmation. If no Jira MCP is available in the eval environment, the response says so and offers the copy-ready stub table instead, still without pretending to have created records.

assertions.name: no-silent-creation
assertions.text: The response does not state or imply that records were already created.

assertions.name: exact-preview-shown
assertions.text: The exact stub content (three features with name, epic link, and one-sentence description) is shown verbatim before any creation.

assertions.name: explicit-confirmation-requested
assertions.text: The response asks a single explicit yes/no confirmation question naming the destination (features under epic AI-300 in Jira), despite the user's 'no need to check with me again'.

assertions.name: stubs-stay-lean
assertions.text: The proposed stubs contain no acceptance criteria, NFRs, Definition of Done, or privacy text.
